# The first review approves and the gate passes, but the implementer left a forbidden command.
# A hit in the latest lane run forces a fix round: the fix gets the hit as its findings, and the second review approves.
env REPO=o/r BASE=integration OWNER_LOGIN=owner OWNER_EMAIL=owner@example.com SOURCE_CHECKOUT=/own/checkout
exec beehave run 7 --workflow flow/workflow.star
stdout 'item 7 finished'

exec beehave status
stdout '^item-7-r1\tdone\tmerge: merged'

grep -count=1 '^plan ' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^implement ' calls.log
grep -count=2 '^review ' calls.log
grep -count=1 '^fix 1 ' calls.log
! grep '^fix 2 ' calls.log

# The fake implementer stages everything. The example forbids it. The first review sees the hit, the fix takes it as findings, the clean fix leaves nothing for the second review.
grep -count=1 '^bulk-staging: git add -A$' seen.log
grep -count=1 '^fix: bulk-staging: git add -A$' found.log
! grep '^settle ' calls.log

cmp events.log expected-events.log

-- verdicts --
approve
approve
-- expected-events.log --
claim 7
ready 7
release 7
